title: A fixed literal evaluates to true on any extension
statement: Let $l$ be a literal on $n$ variables and let $\rho$ be a restriction on those same variables that fixes $l$, meaning $\rho$ assigns $l$'s variable the Boolean value that makes $l$ true. Then for every assignment $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}$, the literal $l$ evaluates to true on the extension of $x$ along $\rho$ (the assignment using $\rho$'s fixed value on each set variable and $x$ on the free ones).
hypotheses_covered: l is a literal on n variables
ρ is a restriction on n variables
ρ fixes l (assigns its variable the value making l true)
x is an arbitrary Boolean assignment
replaced:
If a literal $l$ is fixed by $\rho$, then for every $x$ it evaluates to true on the
extended point: $l.\mathrm{eval}(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x) = \mathrm{true}$.
